Several applied modeling papers (snippets 1, 3) explicitly assume foetuses grow exponentially during gestation, citing Peters (1983), and snippet 10 references a 'fetal growth constant' consistent with exponential-style growth. However, the core DEB-theory sources (Kooijman texts: snippets 5, 6, 8, and especially 12, plus Sous2007 snippet 2) directly contradict pure exponential growth: under DEB, the foetal structural volume follows V(t) = (v·t/3)^3, i.e., a cubic-time growth where weight doubling times increase by 21/3, explicitly noted as 'less steep' than an exponential curve even though it superficially resembles one. Thus the foundational DEB position is that foetal growth approximates but is not truly exponential. The many maternal-obesity/birth-weight clinical snippets (13-24) are off-topic to the functional form of growth. Because the most authoritative theoretical sources contradict strict exponentiality while applied uses adopt it as an approximation, the consensus leans against the literal claim.
